business_scope.primary_industry_name: Proprietary Ultra-Low Latency Algorithmic Market Making

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code with Luxembourg statutory derogations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–China Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement (1983, amended by 2010 protocol)
Luxembourg–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1996, as amended by the 2009 protocol)
Luxembourg–United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention (1967, as amended)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; implementing EU Directives 2015/849, 2018/843, and 2018/843 as transposed; Luxembourg FIU guidance; EU and Luxembourg international sanctions regulations implemented through the Ministry of Finance and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) framework.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the constitutional instrument of each corporate shareholder, including ultimate beneficial owner chart and corporate governance documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or notary in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified passport copy and proof of residential address of each natural person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or current company extract for each corporate shareholder incorporated outside the European Union
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry, chamber of commerce, or Secretary of State in the country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth declaration executed by each UBO, with notarial acknowledgement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Lending or custodial institution in the UBO's jurisdiction, together with a notary public

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated screening of all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories and controlling participants against the consolidated OFAC SDN list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the EU consolidated sanctions list, the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit's internal watchlists, and recognized PEP databases within the meaning of FATF Recommendation 12 and CSSF AML/CFT guidance. Any PEP match requires enhanced due diligence and senior management approval. Negative screening results must be evidenced and retained for at least five years after the relationship ends under the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via https://www.lbr.lu, in coordination with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (R.C.S.)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The full registered name must be written in Latin script, preferably in French, German, or Luxembourgish. Names originally in non-Latin alphabets must be transliterated into Latin characters. The legal entity name for the Société en Commandite Spéciale must include the suffix 'SCSp' or the unabbreviated term 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a written rejection issued by the R.C.S./LBR, the incorporator may within fifteen calendar days file a reasoned administrative appeal to the Ministry of Justice (Direction de l'enregistrement) together with alternative compliant name variants. The Ministry must respond within forty-five calendar days. If the rejection is based solely on a prior conflicting registered name, the applicant may immediately file a revised name application through LBR. Where administrative remedies are exhausted, an appeal may be brought before the administrative court against the registration decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as sole registered office. The SCSp must maintain a genuine, physically situated registered office in Luxembourg. A virtual office service can be used only as an auxiliary mailing address and never as the statutory registered office, particularly because the intended algorithmic high-frequency trading business is subject to statutory licensing, CSSF prudential oversight, and substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated (60–75%). The CSSF and the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit may conduct unannounced on-site inspections within the first year of licensing to verify real business substance, trading operations, co-location of equipment and staff, and the adequacy of internal controls.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT corporate due diligence, PEP and sanctions screening, corporate veil determination, and risk assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee at prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and economic substance consultation, including review of required physical presence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff plus prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (loi concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 102-1 et seq. (SCSp) inserted by the law of 23 July 2016; Grand-Ducal Regulation on commercial register filings
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), attached to the Ministry of Justice, accessible at www.lbr.lu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: First registration application form (formulaire d'immatriculation / dépôt de pièces) filed with RCS together with the full executed limited partnership agreement (contrat de société) constituting the SCSp
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The SCSp is subject to no minimum capital, share-capital or compulsory escrow account; contributions and payment terms are fixed freely in the partnership agreement. Where the partners so agree, initial cash subscriptions may be placed in a segregated Luxembourg bank account pending registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED that: (1) the limited partnership agreement of the SCSp is approved, and the initial capital commitments, profit and loss sharing allocations and subscription rights of the partners are ratified; (2) the registered office of the SCSp is established at [address], Luxembourg; (3) the general partner is confirmed as manager and is authorized, together with the designated officers, to open bank and securities accounts, appoint clearing and payment providers, execute exchange and algorithmic trading agreements and conduct all regulatory filings; (4) designated officers are appointed as representatives before the Luxembourg Business Registers, tax authorities and the CSSF; (5) all steps necessary to incorporate, license and operationalize the SCSp are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability clearance and preliminary AML/KYC pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS and participating accredited professionals; online name-search portal at www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for an RCS name-availability check to ascertain that the proposed SCSp name does not conflict with an existing registered company or trademark. Prepare and execute the drafting mandate for the limited partnership agreement. Collect identification, proof of address, and source-of-wealth documents for every ultimate beneficial owner and the general partner. If any contribution consists of real estate, mandate a Luxembourg notary to prepare the deed.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name and cover letter
Draft SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société)
Passport/ID and proof of residence of each partner
Power of attorney for the legal counsel if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name clearance is denied, resubmit with up to three alternative names and pay a fresh search; if KYC documents are queried, provide certified translations or notarised copies within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarisation of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary for authenticated deed where required; otherwise all partners in private deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene all initial partners, review final terms, and execute the partnership agreement. Include the identification of the sole or lead general partner, the contribution schedule, profit-sharing profile, registered office address, governing law, and scope of algorithmic trading. Have the deed notarised when in-kind contributions or encumbrances over real estate are involved, and obtain certified copies for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Register-office consent and lease or ownership title
Written acceptance of general partner appointment
Notarized copies if notarised route used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial formalities reveal drafting defects, execute a rectification deed or a separate amendment deed before filing, and re-date documents as necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS statutory registration through Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first RCS application through LBR online eFiling; upload scan of executed partnership agreement, general partner identification, and declarations. Verify that any legal filing fee is paid, and request immediate issuance of the RCS extract upon validation. For the SCSp, registration is effected against the general partner because the partnership has no legal personality.
required_dossiers: Identification and residence permits of general partner/managers
Declaration of appointment and registered office consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues a query, correct within fifteen calendar days; file a supplementary declaration to amend the registration data; re-upload notarized documents and expedite the file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, ensure the constitutive excerpt and the appointment of the general partner are transmitted for online publication in RESA. Monitor the publication date because certain third-party effects start only upon RESA publication.
required_dossiers: List of general partner and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA notes an incomplete translation or missing annexes, file a corrected copy via the LBR service desk and republish; only the corrected publication counts for external relations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); direct tax office of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS extract is available, obtain the Luxembourg tax number and VAT number where taxable; register any manager, general partner, or employees with the CCSS; declare the place of effective management and submit substance evidence. Use the RCS extract as proof of formation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT delays registration, request a formal acknowledgment; if an assessment or refusal is issued, submit an administrative appeal to the Director of Registrations or the District Tax Office within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Determination or obtaining of financial-sector authorisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), espace professionnel; ESMA notification for algorithmic trading where financial instruments are traded
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a binding legal mapping of the proprietary HFT and market-making activities under MiFID II. If the activity constitutes regular dealing on own account in financial instruments, file a complete investment-firm authorisation application with CSSF under the law of 5 April 1993; if an exemption applies, document the basis for non-authorisation and keep an internal compliance memorandum. In either case complete CSSF eDesk onboarding.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and copy of partnership deed
Programme of operations and business plan
Risk management and operational resilience policies
AML/CFT policy and designation of AML officer
Fit and proper declarations for directors/general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CSSF sends a deficiency letter, respond within ten business days; if the activity is outside authorisation scope, provide an independent legal opinion and, where necessary, apply for an ESMA/MiFID passport notification; if refused, exercise administrative appeal and court review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Clearing, settlement and LEI operational configuration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Clearing institutions and settlement systems accepted in Luxembourg, exchange/CCP membership desks, and GLEIF for LEI registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open clearing, prime-brokerage, or direct membership accounts and arrange segregated cash and securities accounts; complete all counterparty KYC and onboarding; register or renew the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) under GLEIF; map target payment rails, including direct exchange clearing and Fedwire, and configure minimum collateral requirements; confirm the SCSp may lawfully use the chosen rails based on its CSSF status or exemption.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening and KYC package
Luxembourg legal opinion on enforceability if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a clearinghouse or payment rail provider refuses access, update the due-diligence pack, obtain an updated legal opinion from Luxembourg counsel, or add a licensed general partner as co-signatory; if LEI validation fails, correct reference data through GLEIF.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), with notification and coordination by ESMA under MiFID II for algorithmic trading; Ministry of Finance for Luxembourg financial-sector policy; Administration de l'environnement for physical environmental permits; Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) and Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) for occupational and fire clearances
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Investment firm authorisation (agrément d'entreprise d'investissement) under Luxembourg law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, as amended, covering MiFID II Annex I Section A activity 'Dealing on Own Account'; alternatively a documented exemption and, where applicable, exchange/CCP direct-membership recognition

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement – Luxembourg Environment Agency, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory EIA and screening because the activity is a quant/office-technology use not listed in national EIA annexes; a municipal building permit and, where applicable, an environmental class permit for server-room cooling and emergency generators are required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater in normal trading operations; domestic sewage must comply with municipal sewer discharge by-laws. E-waste, including servers, network equipment, and UPS batteries, must be disposed through an approved Luxembourg processor in accordance with EU Directive 2012/19/EU on WEEE and Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries. Refrigerant use must comply with F-gas Regulation (EU) No 517/2014. Emergency generators and combustion equipment must satisfy Luxembourg general air emission and immission standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval from the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) and the Inspection générale de la protection civile; structural load certificate for floors and racks in server and trading rooms issued by a Luxembourg licensed engineering bureau; electrical safety certification and workplace ergonomics, lighting, and emergency-exit checks under the Luxembourg Labour Code; occupational safety validation from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg direct tax authority; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Luxembourg VAT and indirect tax authority; unified e-portal: MyGuichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For foreign entities, obtain a Luxembourg business registration number ('numéro d'immatriculation' / RCS number) by registering with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through MyGuichet.lu (or via a notary or certified agent). Upon RCS registration, the Luxembourg tax administration automatically assigns a national identification number (matricule d'identification) for tax purposes. Before commencing VAT-taxable activities in Luxembourg, foreign non-established entities must register for VAT via the VAT registration desk of the AEDT, using form No. 1000/1 (VAT registration form) submitted electronically or through a tax representative; a Luxembourg VAT ID (prefixed 'LU') is issued after the tax office validates the application. If the entity makes only B2B supplies subject to reverse charge or supplies outside Luxembourg, registration may not be required; however, an SCSp carrying on trading as a fixed base in Luxembourg will generally need to register for Luxembourg direct taxes (corporate/income tax and municipal business tax) as it will be transparent with partners taxed individually.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' election; the SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent and has no separate tax personality. No election to be taxed as a corporation is available for an SCSp (unless it is a commercial company under a different civil form). However, tax elections may arise under the Tax Code in relation to partnership filing: the SCSp itself is not taxable, but partners may elect to allocate Luxembourg-source income only if they hold beneficial interest. Also, hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD transposed) require an analysis when the foreign partner's home jurisdiction treats the SCSp as opaque; no elective elimination of a hybrid mismatch is permitted, but Luxembourg has optional application of CIT grouping rules (intégration fiscale) only for corporate entities, not partnerships. There is no direct election for the SCSp to be treated as a transparent entity in another country; tax-treaty and EU law shape recognition.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual taxable turnover excluding VAT) for Luxembourg-established small businesses under Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; for foreign entities with no establishment in Luxembourg, there is no registration threshold – a VAT registration obligation arises as soon as they make taxable supplies in Luxembourg unless the customer self-assesses the tax under the reverse-charge mechanism.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance (no e-invoicing transmission obligation, no API/digital stamping) for B2B or B2C invoices. E-invoicing may be used voluntarily if the authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility are ensured (VAT Directive compliance). E-invoicing to Luxembourg public authorities (B2G) is compulsory under Directive 2014/55/EU via the Luxembourg e-invoicing platform. VAT returns (ELMA) and annual recapitulative statements (Intrastat/ECS) are filed electronically on MyGuichet.lu; no continuous transaction control (CTC) or SAF-T filing is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the European Union qualify for zero-rated supply (0% VAT) provided the export is evidenced by transport documentation and the goods physically leave EU territory within statutory time limits (usually 3 months from supply). For outbound services (including algorithmic trading and financial services) supplied to a customer outside the EU: (i) if the customer is a business (taxable person), the place of supply is the customer's jurisdiction under the B2B rule, and no Luxembourg VAT is charged; (ii) if the customer is a non-taxable person outside the EU, the supply is generally outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (non-taxation), or may be exempt if it qualifies as a financial service. To claim zero-rating on exports of goods, the supplier must hold and submit proof of export to the AEDT: customs export declaration (SAD), transport documents (B/L or AWB), and commercial invoices; a written declaration or certificate from the carrier may also be required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document – Electronic export declaration via Luxembourg customs/ECS)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR transport document evidencing physical departure from the EU
Commercial invoice and proof of payment (bank transfer/Inward Remittance Certificate where relevant)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT conducts targeted audits on zero-rating claims, requiring full documentary evidence within prescribed time limits. If the supplier fails to obtain export certification within 90 days (or the extended periods provided by the Grand-Ducal Regulation), the zero-rated supply is retrospectively clawed back to taxable status at the standard rate (17%); the taxpayer is liable for VAT, late interest (at the annual statutory rate of 3.6% on the VAT due) and may face penalties under Article 11 of the Luxembourg Tax Adjustment Law and Articles 512/513 of the VAT Law. Fraudulent misuse of zero-rating (false declarations, fake export documents, falsified proof of transport) is criminal tax fraud, punishable by fines up to EUR 250,000 (or 50% of the evaded tax), imprisonment (1–5 years), and publication of the judgment; civil penalties of up to 200% of the tax evaded may be imposed. In addition, all partners of the transparent SCSp may be held jointly liable if the fraud was committed for the benefit of the partnership.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting as an Eurosystem member together with the European Central Bank, with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the competent national regulator for banking conduct, AML/CFT enforcement, payment services licensing, and foreign-exchange transaction monitoring in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg uses the euro as its sole legal tender and is fully bound by the EU Treaty provisions on the free movement of capital and payments (Articles 63 to 66 TFEU). There is a complete absence of exchange controls, prior administrative authorisations, or quantitative limits on current-account or capital-account transactions. Profit remittance by non-resident partners of a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) is unrestricted; the SCSp is fiscally transparent so its trading gains flow through to partners without Luxembourg withholding tax, subject only to CRS/FATCA reporting and AML/KYC scrutiny. Transfer of funds in EUR via SEPA/TARGET2 and in foreign currency via SWIFT is wholly liberalised, provided the account-holding bank satisfies EU financial sanctions (OFAC/EU asset-freeze) and CSSF transaction-monitoring obligations. No exchange-rate approval, no investment screening, and no local-financing ratio apply to proprietary algorithmic trading capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable: Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, no repatriation timeline, and no requirement to liquidate foreign-currency receivables into EUR. The SCSp's proprietary HFT and market-making activity under ISIC 6499 / NAICS 523130 generates no physical-export documentary collections; therefore the partnership may lawfully retain, hold, and reinvest any EUR or foreign-currency balances freely. In the event of future service fees charged to non-resident counterparties, such receivables may likewise remain in the currency of choice without declaration to the BCL and without ECB balance-of-payments reporting beyond the standard statistical thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority_note: Not part of the schema but retained as an explicit fact: BCL and CSSF jointly supervise payment and securities settlement; however, the SCSp is not a regulated credit institution and requires no BCL licence as long as it confines itself to proprietary trading on own account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Collateral Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Prime Brokerage Settlement Account
Prime Brokerage Cash Account / Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM as principal treasury utility, MEDIUM as auxiliary low-value payment channel. The CSSF authorises Electronic Money Institutions and Payment Institutions under Luxembourg laws implementing PSD2 and EMD2, and EU/EEA-licensed EMIs may passport into Luxembourg. However, EMIs are not credit institutions: they may not accept deposits, cannot provide the segregated collateral, exchange-membership margin, prime-brokerage or settlement guarantees required for ultra-low-latency algorithmic market making, and their own counterparty-risk profile is generally incompatible with the SCSp's daily settlement volumes. An EMI may be used only for small operational disbursements if it operates under a full EU banking passport relationship, holds client funds safeguarded by a Tier-1 EU bank, executes wire transfers exclusively via SWIFT MT103/TARGET2, and contractually disclaims any margin or collateral custodial function. Blueprint recommendation: rely on the Tier-1 bank relationship for all material treasury flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The definitive Luxembourg standard requires the SCSp's general partner (gérant), the signatories, and the ultimate beneficial owners to attend one physical onboarding meeting at the bank's Luxembourg head office or a recognised EU branch, followed by a mandatory compliance interview recorded and minuted by the bank's AML/KYC officer. Post-COVID CSSF circular guidance permits video-identification for certain low-risk retail cases, yet Tier-1 banks uniformly retain the physical-interview mandate for a scoped entity presenting non-resident partners, third-party management of trading activities, and high-turnover account classification. Exceptions to physical appearance exist only where (i) the bank has an existing prime-brokerage or fund-administrator relationship with the sponsor, and (ii) video identification is fully remediated with notarised, apostilled, and professional-translated corporate documents compliant with the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, Article 3-2. Onboarding timeline under the physical-interview track: five to eight weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp beneficial-ownership opacity: as a transparent partnership without legal personality, the SCSp creates ambiguity in the attribution of legal and beneficial ownership, and the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) may lag behind changes in partner composition for special limited partnerships.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (i) certified extracts of the Luxembourg RBE registration (registration number and filing date); (ii) the notarised or registered partnership deed and a subsequent deed of amendments; (iii) an ownership-netting exemplification chart to the natural-person level identifying each partner's share percentage and the entity's LEI; (iv) for corporate partners, their constitutional documents, board resolutions approving the subscription, and UBO declarations in the standard bank format; (v) a Luxembourg legal opinion from an eligible avocat confirming the absence of bearer shares, nominee arrangements, and any concealment in the SCSt structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth/source of funds versus projected HFT volumes: the expected ultra-high transaction frequency, the size of the initial capital injection (EUR 5M to 20M), and the velocity of operations are inconsistent with standard visible wealth profiles of the individual partners, triggering enhanced due diligence and wealth-origin reconstruction requests.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a partner-by-partner source-of-wealth file: audited financial statements for the last three financial years of corporate contributors, personal tax assessments of individuals, bank reference letters and MT103 wire records from the remitting institutions, evidence of historical proprietary trading audited by an independent third party, the trading track record with P&L statements, exchange membership or licensing certificates of any predecessor vehicle, and a narrative memorandum explaining the accumulation of capital. All documents to be notarised/apostilled and professionally translated into French or English.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdictional counterparty risk in the clearing network: counterparties located in OFAC/EU-sanctioned or high-risk territories, shell-bank reliance, dark-pool execution venues, or payment chains that layer multiple intermediary correspondent banks will trigger the bank's transaction-monitoring system and may block the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) an execution-venue whitelist with legal names and LEIs of the exchanges, CCPs, and prime brokers, explicitly excluding sanctioned venues (Eurex, Euronext, Xetra, CME, and similar regulated venues only); (ii) an executed ISDA/CSA and prime-brokerage agreement suite evidencing that settlement is centralised on TARGET2, CLS, SWIFT MT103, Fedwire and/or CHIPS, without intermediary shell banks; (iii) a sanctions-screening policy document, negative screening results, and the MLRO's certificate; (iv) the SCSp's AML/KYC internal policy, approved by the gérant, showing automated screening of all wire instructions against EU, UN, OFAC and CSSF lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory-activity concern: the bank may suspect that the SCSp is performing regulated 'investment services' or 'systematic internalising' requiring a MiFID II/CSSF license rather than falling strictly within proprietary trading on own account for ISIC 6499.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce (i) a CSSF confirmation letter or a professional legal opinion applying MiFID II Annex I exclusions to the SCSp business model; (ii) the partnership deed stating that all orders are executed exclusively for the account and at the risk of the partnership, with profits distributed pro-rata to partners; (iii) the trading governance manual with pre-trade risk limits and algo-circuit-breaker documentation; (iv) confirmation that no client orders or third-party assets are handled; (v) a CSSF fit-and-proper attestation by the designated officer confirming that the activity is outside CSSF authorisation and that no investor-compensation regime applies — enabling the bank to classify the SCSp as a standard institutional treasury customer rather than a high-risk financial institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound partner capital must reach the SCSp's Tier-1 Luxembourg account exclusively through SWIFT MT103 in EUR to the beneficiary's IBAN/BIC of the Luxembourg branch, with the purpose field (Tag 70) citing: 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — SCSP PARTNERSHIP SUBSCRIPTION'. For EEA-sourced EUR, a SEPA Credit Transfer with the ISO purpose code 'CAPC' or 'COMC' is acceptable; for USD-sourced capital, route via Fedwire or CHIPS to the Luxembourg bank's New York correspondent with narrative referencing the SCSp LEI, the partnership deed date, and the partner's capital-account identifier. Each injection above EUR 100,000 requires the bank's prior green-light verification of the remitter's updated KYC file; aggregate deposits above EUR 1M per calendar day trigger the CSSF statutory transaction-monitoring UBO confirmation. There is no CSSF/Bcl authorisation threshold for capital import, no economic-approval requirement, and no ECB exchange-control filing; the bank must nevertheless record the equity versus shareholder-loan character under Luxembourg thin-capitalisation and TBI (transfer-pricing) rules for its internal accounting classification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Execution follows four clearing rails: (1) TARGET2 RTGS for all EUR-denominated payments to exchanges, central counterparties and the prime broker, providing finality and immediate availability of liquidity; (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-TARGET2 counterparties and for manual start-of-day / end-of-day funding balances; (3) Fedwire and CHIPS for USD margin calls and USD-cleared derivative settlements; (4) CLS (Continuous Linked Settlement) for foreign-exchange legs, including the EUR/USD and EUR/GBP flows generated by hedging instruments, thereby eliminating Herstatt risk. Commercial Letters of Credit are not used in this HFT model; instead trade disbursements are structured as prime-brokerage daily margin transfers, CCP variation-margin settlements through Euroclear/ Clearstream, and netted ISDA payments, all implemented as straight-through processing segregated by sub-account between partner capital and proprietary trading capital. Every outbound message must carry the trade-purpose narrative code ('MARGIN TRANSFER', 'TRADE SETTLEMENT', 'TREASURY PLACEMENT' or 'FX HEDGE SETTLEMENT') and be retained in the CSSF-required transaction-monitoring log with a 10-year record-retention policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards for the liquid G10 pairs (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, EUR/JPY, EUR/AUD) with tenors up to 12 months, executed under the ISDA 1998 FX Definitions and covered by the Prime Brokerage CSA, used purely to neutralise the grid exposure accumulating from market-making in multiple instruments and currencies.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to emerging-market currencies where physical delivery is impossible or legally impractical (USD/CNH, USD/KRW, USD/INR, USD/BRL), settled against the ECB or Reuters fixings, with ISDA documentation and CLS settlement where available.

Cross-currency swaps (XCY currency interest-rate swaps) for two-leg notional and coupon exchange in EUR versus USD, GBP, or JPY, applied to matched-funding of long-term margin balances and strategic counterparty financing, cleared via LCH SwapClear or EurexOTC Clear, thereby achieving CVA-risk reduction.

Exchange-traded FX futures on Eurex and CME for intra-daily delta hedging of the inventory, eligible without any CSSF authorisation because all trading is for the SCSp's own account and is classified as a treasury hedging activity under Annex I of the partnership deed.

FX options (vanilla, and barrier options in limited circumstances) written by a licensed EU/EEA or Swiss bank, confined to risk-reduction strategies directly referable to the net open currency exposure arising from the algorithmic portfolio and not for speculative yield-seeking.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end; calendar-year SCSp: by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-imposed fine up to EUR 10,000; publication of the judgment; personal liability of managing partners; repeated non-filing may result in administrative removal from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO annual confirmation and transfer-driven update (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RBE service of the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation no later than the filing date of the annual accounts; any UBO change, including transfers of partnership interests, declared within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines per breach (EUR 2,500-EUR 10,000); criminal prosecution for knowingly false declarations, with fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income / municipal business / net wealth tax filings (transparent allocation schedule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - Luxembourg tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due 30 June following the end of the tax year; extension available on written request; calendar-year SCSp usually files by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; assessment surcharges up to 10%; ex officio assessment where no return is filed; tax criminal penalties for fraudulent omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual CSSF regulatory and prudential submissions (applicable CSSF license regime for algorithmic market-making)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual prudential and conduct-of-business reports per applicable CSSF circular or regulation, typically within 4 months after financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative sanctions, fines, license suspension or withdrawal, and periodic penalty payments for non-compliance with CSSF reporting obligations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (reviseur d'entreprises agree) where the SCSp exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average employees 25. Audit is also triggered if RCS transparency rules require accounts publication or if partners holding at least 50% of capital or voting rights so request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP per the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts (transposition of EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS permitted for consolidated and supervised financial entities; annual accounts filed in the required format prescribed for partnerships.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must identify every beneficial owner holding more than 25% of partnership interests or voting rights, or exercising control by other means. After transfers of partnership interests, UBO data must be updated with the RBE within 30 days. An annual confirmation of accuracy is aligned with the annual reporting cycle and lodged no later than the annual accounts filing. The general partner is legally responsible for maintaining the register and confirming that UBO records reflect current shareholding.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (partnership interests and transfer history)
Register of Directors (general partners and managers)
Minute Book (partner resolutions and annual general decisions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Luxembourg SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale) is fiscally transparent by default and is not itself subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT); profits are attributed and taxed at partner level. A resident corporate partner bears the aggregate Luxembourg corporate burden of 24.94% (CIT 17% plus 7% solidarity surcharge plus Luxembourg-City municipal business tax of 6.75%). Targeted incentives include: (i) 100% participation exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains (Art. 166 LIR); (ii) 80% exemption of net qualifying IP-box income (Art. 50ter LIR), only for patented or equivalently protected software qualifying as IP within the nexus rules; (iii) R&D tax credit against CIT; (iv) optional arm's length grouping benefits; and (v) entity-level CIT election may be available where the partnership opts to be treated as an opaque collective entity, subject to the statutory 24.94% rate and to net wealth tax.
